subject: psychiatry
title: Suicide and deliberate self-harm

steps.tx: **Suicide** is self inflicted death with intent to die, while deliberate self-harm includes self poisoning and self injury regardless of suicidal intent, though repetition strongly predicts later suicide. Most who die by suicide have a treatable mental disorder (depression, bipolar, schizophrenia, substance use) compounded by hopelessness, though risk prediction in individuals remains statistically poor: risk factors stratify groups, they do not predict persons, so care rests on formulation and modifiable needs, not scores alone.
steps.say: Self harm and suicide overlap but differ in intent. Scores cannot predict a person: formulate needs and treat illness.

steps.tx: Assessment explores ideation (passive death wish versus active plans), intent, **means access**, preparatory acts, past attempts (especially high lethality or violent methods), hopelessness, reasons for living, substance intoxication, psychosis commanding harm, recent losses, discharge or service transitions, and protective relationships. Asking directly about suicide does not implant the idea and is mandatory after self-harm. Collateral and records correct minimisation.
steps.say: Ask plainly: thoughts, plans, means, past acts, hope, protection. Asking does not plant suicide.

steps.tx: **Key point.** Highest risk periods are the weeks after psychiatric discharge, after self-harm presentations, and in early psychosis and severe depression with agitation, insomnia and alcohol use. Men die more often (lethal methods), women attempt more often. Older men, single or bereaved status, chronic pain and illness, unemployment and access to firearms, pesticides or high places form recurring exam patterns. Previous attempt is the strongest single predictor of future death.
steps.say: Weeks after discharge are deadliest. A past attempt predicts future death strongest.

steps.tx: Management treats underlying illness vigorously (antidepressants with follow up, lithium in bipolar disorder and clozapine in schizophrenia both reduce suicide specifically), restricts means (medication quantities, firearm and pesticide access, bridge barriers), builds collaborative **safety plans** (warning signs, internal coping, contacts, professional help, means safety), ensures rapid post discharge follow up within days, and involves family with consent. Compulsory admission applies when legal criteria of risk and disorder meet, as last resort therapeutic frame, not prediction proof.
steps.say: Treat illness, remove means, plan safety, follow up in days. Lithium and clozapine cut suicide specifically.
